newsitem.title: USA: Former Centennial CEO denied bail.
newsitem.headline: Former Centennial CEO denied bail.

text.p: A U.S. magistrate denied bail on Friday for former Centennial Technologies Inc Chief Executive Emanuel Pinez, held behind bars on securities fraud charges, a court clerk said.
U.S. District Court Magistrate Lawrence Cohen ordered Pinez, 58, detained pending trial, a court clerk for Cohen told Reuters.
Cohen said in his ruling that Pinez, an Israeli citizen with family in Israel and Switzerland, "has all the incentive to flee (the country) and none to remain."

"By remaining, he faces almost certain conviction and deportation. By fleeing, on the other hand, he will have found a safe haven from prosecution - not to mention a haven to which funds have been transmitted in the past," Cohen wrote.
If convicted, Pinez faces imprisonment of from 37 to 47 months, Cohen wrote, for insider trading stemming from his alleged transactions in put and call orders on Centennial stock.

Cohen also wrote that Pinez was convicted of a copyright offense in Switzerland in 1987 and fined $5,000. According to Pinez, Cohen wrote, he received probation for the charge, which was later expunged.

Last week, Centennial fired Pinez, who founded the company in 1987, and the manufacturer of personal computer cards said it was checking the accuracy of its financial reports for 1996 and the first half of 1997.
Pinez allegedly manipulated inventories to inflate Centennial's revenues to match analysts expectations, according to court documents.

According to an affidavit filed in court Friday by Robert Turgiss, a special agent with the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Pinez admitted to the Centennial board of directors shortly before he was fired that he lent customers his own money to allow them to buy goods in excess of their needs.

Pinez did not say directly how much of his own money he lent to customers, but mentioned a $10 million figure in the context of the discussion, Turgiss said. In some instances, the customers did not receive the shipment of goods, according to the affadavit.
Pinez has been held in a Plymouth, Mass. jail since his arrest.
